news.title: Binance Restores Withdrawals Across 87 Networks After Reported $6.3 Billion Theft
news.body: Binance said on November 14 that it had reopened withdrawals across 87 networks after a late-October attack; PYMNTS puts the theft at approximately $6.3 billion. Binance says corporate funds and emergency reserves will cover customer losses, but replacing balances does not restore customers’ ability to transfer every asset. The exchange targeted restoration of remaining networks and assets by the end of the following week. Treasury counterparties should check asset-level withdrawal availability and transfer limits before treating access as fully restored.

news.title: Three Central Banks Test Coordinated FX Settlement Across Different Payment Systems
news.body: The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Bank of Thailand published tests of synchronized payment-versus-payment and multilateral net FX settlement across RTGS and distributed-ledger environments. The results demonstrate technical coordination across different systems, not a live service or proven corridor-level savings. Settlement banks evaluating participation should focus on legal finality, operating hours and liquidity requirements ahead of the Bank of England’s planned synchronization interface in 2028.

news.title: Metro Bank Opens Sale Process Despite Having No Active Buyer Talks
news.body: Metro Bank launched a strategic review including a formal sale process after reporting 37% loan growth, while saying it had no active discussions with potential buyers. The process puts its current-account relationships, business lending and distribution in play for potential consolidation, but no bidder or valuation establishes a likely outcome. Business customers and payment suppliers should track bidder disclosures and any proposed changes to account servicing, technology contracts and payment-service continuity.

news.title: Stolen-Card Rental Scheme Leaves Legitimate Merchants Exposed After Delivering the Service
news.body: Dumpster Rental Enterprises reported 312 stolen-card orders in 2026, versus 15 in 2024, describing scammers who collect renters’ payments and use stolen cards to pay legitimate suppliers. Merchants can complete the rental and still receive a cardholder dispute; the figures describe one broker, not industry-wide losses. Rental firms and their acquirers can target checks at renter-cardholder mismatches and repeated card attempts before dispatch, rather than discovering the mismatch after service delivery.

news.title: CSI Integrates Acquired Payment Tools to Expand Community Banks’ Commercial Offering
news.body: CSI CEO Nancy Langer said the company has integrated acquired Qolo and Apiture capabilities into its core platform, including cash management, payment orchestration, virtual accounts and real-time account ledgers. That gives community banks access to more commercial-payment functionality through an existing core relationship rather than a separate vendor purchase. Banks assessing the offering should request live deployment references, migration requirements and implementation timelines before counting on deposit retention or new business-account revenue.

perspective: Today: Binance restores withdrawals and Metro Bank seeks a buyer, alongside cross-border settlement tests, merchant fraud and community-bank payment integration.

curiosity.text: In 1998, the U.S. Federal Reserve began offering FedACH International, enabling banks to send cross-border ACH payments through the U.S. ACH network to participating destinations. The service uses local clearing systems abroad for the final leg, so a payment can cross borders without every bank needing a direct international connection. Source: Federal Reserve Financial Services, “FedACH International” — https://www.frbservices.org/financial-services/ach/fedach-international
